Subject: MAP kickoff — Atlas Bio private deployment & evaluation timeline

Hi Samira / Rajiv —

Thanks for the demo last week. As discussed, I’m opening a short mutual action plan (MAP) thread to align owners, milestones, and the timeline for a private/VPC deployment evaluation. I’ve attached a starter MAP spreadsheet (Atlas_MAP_v1.xlsx) — please review and comment.

High-level asks from our side so we can get a firm plan in motion:
- Confirm primary networking/VPN contact at Atlas and whether you prefer AWS PrivateLink, Site-to-Site VPN, or a dedicated transit approach.
- Confirm IAM and KMS owner who will own key provisioning, rotation, and access control for the eval environment.
- Confirm the target evaluation window and procurement close date (we penciled 2027-01-15 as the goal in the proposal).
- Share any org constraints (allowed IP ranges, approved CAs, HSM/KMS vendor constraints).

Proposed cadence / milestones in the attached sheet (editable):
1) Week 0: MAP & role alignment (this thread)
2) Week 1–2: Network connectivity & IAM/KMS setup (smoke test)
3) Week 3: Performance + latency evaluation with 2 sample workloads
4) Week 4: Security questionnaire and SOC2 evidence pass-through
5) Week 5: Decision/close or follow-on pilot

Can we do a 45-minute kickoff call next week? I’m available Tues/Wed afternoon PST. If you prefer, suggest two slots and we’ll lock something.

Cc’ing our infra and security owners — priyom, kimberly, and mateo — who will own parts of the plan on the Redwood side.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Olga Petrov

Hi all —

Couple of technical constraints from our side before we lock dates:
- Firewall/NAT: we have a set of outbound IP ranges that are locked down. Can you confirm if Redwood supports static egress IPs for the eval nodes, or whether we should expect ephemeral IPs behind NAT?
- Connectivity preference: PrivateLink is preferred for control-plane traffic; we’ll use Site-to-Site VPN for heavier data flows initially. Do you support BGP on the VPN endpoints and can you expose a test BGP peer?
- KMS: we use AWS KMS but require that customer-managed CMKs be used for production. For the eval we can provision a temporary key, but want to validate key policy and encryption-in-transit expectations.

If you can share a minimal architecture diagram with IP ranges and a sample cloudformation/terraform snippet for endpoint creation, that would speed the network team review.

Thanks — Rajiv
Cloud Infrastructure Manager | Atlas Bio
rajiv.menon@atlasbio.com

Hi Rajiv / Samira —

I’ll take point for IAM & KMS on the Redwood side for the eval. Quick checklist so we have alignment:
- KMS: for the eval we can provision customer-managed CMKs in your account or use a Redwood-managed key with access controls; for production we recommend customer CMKs + HSM-backed keys.
- IAM roles: we’ll provide a minimal set of cross-account roles (read-only deploy and monitoring) and a provisioning role for the initial setup. Please share an account-id for cross-account role trust.
- Key rotation & audit: we’ll enable key rotation and exportable CloudTrail logs for key usage. Please note HSM-backed rotation will take 24–48 hours to propagate policies.

I’ve attached a SOC2 evidence request we typically use for evaluations — it lists the specific artifacts we’ll need when you get to the security review step.

Timing: if Procurement needs signatures by Jan 20, we’ll aim to complete connectivity & KMS prove-out by Dec 22 so the security review can proceed in the final week of December.

Thanks — Kimberly
